clue.text: Daunting challenge for an aspiring lawyer — or an alcoholic?

definitions.text: Daunting challenge for an aspiring lawyer
definitions.meaning: first meaning: getting through the exam that qualifies you to practise law

definitions.note: elliptical: read as the daunting challenge for an alcoholic
definitions.meaning: second meaning: walking past a pub without going in

explanation.walkthrough: The bar is both the legal profession and a place that serves drinks, so the same phrase is the lawyer's exam and the drinker's test of willpower.
explanation.definitionFit: To be admitted to the profession a would-be attorney must succeed at the qualifying exam, which is the phrase's everyday sense.

clue.text: Sibyl returns on the radio

indicators.note: what is on the radio is only heard, so the answer is judged by its sound

parts.note: returns on an investment are its profit

explanation.surface: An announcer named Sibyl comes back to the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sibyl' looks like a woman's first name; in the classical world a sibyl was a woman who foretold the future.
explanation.definitionFit: The sibyls were prophetesses of ancient Greece and Rome, oracles who spoke for the gods.

clue.text: Cake sis baked will make you nauseous

indicators.note: baking transforms the raw mixture, so the letters come out in a new form

parts.note: the two words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A warning that your sister's homemade cake will turn your stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasickness is the queasiness caused by a boat's motion, so seasick means feeling sick to the stomach.

clue.text: What we aim for when you cut?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a standard of perfection to strive towards

definitions.note: read as a reply: when you cut the deck, I deal
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: at cards, once you have cut the deck

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into I DEAL: in card games one player cuts the pack and the other deals.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect standard or goal, the thing people strive to reach.

clue.text: McDonald's' most basic need: street-level buzzer, loud

parts.note: street level is the ground floor
a bee buzzes
f is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A burger chain's essentials seem to include a loud doorbell at the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' suggests a doorbell; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced beef is the raw material of every hamburger, the fast-food chain's most fundamental ingredient.

clue.text: Successor heard a song

indicators.note: heard means the word is listened to, not read, so a same-sounding spelling is wanted

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: The next in line was heard singing.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir inherits a title or estate, succeeding the previous holder.

clue.text: Suppression aplenty in Indian city

parts.note: a ban suppresses something
galore means in abundance

explanation.surface: Censorship is everywhere in a city of India.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's official name is now Bengaluru.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore is the capital of Karnataka in southern India, known for its technology industry.

clue.text: Expanses with pines once again?

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
to pine for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Wide stretches of land are planted with conifers for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' looks like trees beside the expanses; it is the verb meaning yearns.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaches are long stretches of land or water, such as the straight part of a river.

clue.text: Fix broken plates

indicators.note: something broken has its pieces scattered, so they go back together in a new order

parts.note: the word used letter for letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to mend smashed crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To staple papers is to fasten or attach them with a wire clip.

clue.text: Speak of zero value

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
to rate something is to value it

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about something that is worth nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, a grander synonym for speaking.

clue.text: Madcap LA notions that can add spice to things

definitions.text: that can add spice to things
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun: something that can add spice

indicators.note: something madcap is wild and reckless, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: the abbreviation for Los Angeles plus the word notions, used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Crazy Hollywood ideas are the kind that liven things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice' tempts you to read the Los Angeles notions as figurative zest; the definition is literal seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Onion salt is a seasoning blend of dried onion and salt, sprinkled on food for flavour.

clue.text: Chief of Houston transportation company — one that's susceptible to recession?

indicators.note: the chief of something is its head, so only the opening letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of Houston
a company that carries passengers by plane

explanation.surface: The Houston boss of a transport firm is the one most exposed when the economy turns down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recession' looks economic, but the definition means receding, as a hairline does when a man goes bald.
explanation.definitionFit: The front edge of the hair on a man's head often moves back with age, which is called receding.

clue.text: Server to cut around tart's filling

indicators.note: around says one word goes round the outside of the other

parts.note: to chop is to cut

indicators.note: the filling of a pie is what sits in its middle, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of tart

explanation.surface: A waiter is told to slice round the middle of a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: A carhop is an American term for a server at a drive-in restaurant who brings food out to customers in their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A carhop is a waiter or waitress serving customers seated in their parked cars.

clue.text: Type of book chain is in for retrospective

indicators.note: is in says one piece sits inside another
retrospective means looking back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
a manacle is a chain for the wrists

explanation.surface: A bookshop chain is putting on a retrospective of one kind of book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain' suggests a bookshop chain, and 'for' looks like a link word, but it supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A roman à clef is a novel in which real people appear thinly disguised as fictional characters, a genre of fiction.

clue.text: Souvenir, like a gift from Barbie perhaps?

parts.note: a gift tag begins with to, followed by the recipient
Ken is the boyfriend doll of Barbie, so her present would be addressed to him

explanation.surface: A keepsake that resembles a present from a famous doll.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: a present from Barbie would carry a tag reading 'to Ken'.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a small object kept as a reminder, much like a souvenir or memento.

clue.text: In Borneo, "log" is Malaysian term of recent vintage

indicators.note: in says the word sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: A note on a Malaysian word for a log used on the island of Borneo.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression, one that has only recently come into use.

clue.text: Population of idiots to show contempt for Western capital, suppressing a hint of intelligence

parts.note: to boo is to jeer at someone

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: Boise is the capital of Idaho, a western US state

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of intelligence

explanation.surface: A sneer at the dim citizens of a western state capital, who lack even a trace of brains.
explanation.walkthrough: Booboisie is H. L. Mencken's coinage, a blend of boob and bourgeoisie, for the stupid general public.
explanation.definitionFit: Mencken coined the word for the mass of uneducated, gullible people, a whole class of boobs or fools.

clue.text: "Father Time" comes after such a serial

indicators.note: comes after fixes the running order, so the earlier words follow the later ones

parts.note: so plus a, taken as written with such read as so
pop is an informal word for father
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: The old man with the scythe follows that kind of drama on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father Time' looks like one figure but splits into father and time; 'such a' supplies the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running broadcast drama in episodes, the classic example of a serial.

clue.text: Cross Kentucky with one of our gang?

parts.note: a bridge spans a river, which means it crosses it
KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A question about crossbreeding something from Kentucky with a member of our crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like crossbreeding, but it is a verb meaning bridge. Our Gang was a series of 1920s-40s comedy shorts about a group of children, also known as The Little Rascals.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanky McFarland played the chubby ringleader of the child actors in the Our Gang films; the question mark admits the lowercase disguise.

clue.text: In fact, Southerner misbehaves

indicators.note: in says the word sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: The truth is that a man from the South is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fact' reads as a set phrase meaning actually, but 'In' is the signal and 'fact' starts the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out is to behave badly, especially as an expression of hidden feelings, as children do.

clue.text: Uncredited actor appears in complex tragedy

indicators.note: appears in says the word shows up inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A bit-part player is cast in a complicated tragic drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a film or stage performer in a crowd scene, usually with no line and no screen credit.

clue.text: Bug in pursuit of chewed-up tree, for the most part!

definitions.text: Bug in pursuit of chewed-up tree, for the most part!

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following behind, so this piece comes after the other
something chewed up is mangled, so the letters are jumbled
for the most part means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
a mite is a tiny bug

explanation.surface: An insect is busy with a tree it has gnawed nearly away.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: an insect that chews wood until most of a tree is gone, hence the exclamation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are wood-eating insects that hollow out timber and trees from within.

clue.text: Goddess is tamer, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters fall into a different order

parts.note: the two words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A regretful note that a goddess has become less wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek deity of the hunt and wild animals, twin sister of Apollo.

clue.text: King, for example, and god chasing gold

indicators.note: something chasing follows behind, so this piece is placed after the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A monarch and a deity hunt for treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' suggests royalty, but it is Stephen King, the horror novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen King is a best-selling writer, so he is one example of a writer of books.

clue.text: Largely guarantee assessment of diamonds in a card game

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to back something is to support or guarantee it
gems are weighed and graded in carats

explanation.surface: Valuing gems more or less guarantees a place in a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds' suggests the card suit, but here it means the gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino gambling game played with playing cards, famously favoured by James Bond.

clue.text: Start to curtail brute's influence

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of curtail
a lout is a rough, brutish man

explanation.surface: An effort to begin limiting a thug's power.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after brute stands for is, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout means power or sway over others, as in political clout.

clue.text: Suffering in European country with loss of leadership

indicators.note: losing its leader means the word's head, its first letter, is removed

parts.note: a country in south-western Europe

explanation.surface: Hardship in a European nation after its government falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is physical or mental distress, a close synonym of suffering.

clue.text: Wise guy's awkward wait amid rise

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a knoll is a small hill or rise in the ground

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy and out of shape, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A smart alec is stuck waiting uncomfortably while something goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after guy stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise guy is a smart alec who acts as though he understands everything, which is a know-it-all.

clue.text: Drug would be 3 if I were Tim

indicators.note: if one thing were another, the first is swapped out and the second put in its place

parts.note: 3-down's answer means perfect; another word for that is optimum
the letter taken as written
the name taken as written

explanation.surface: A cross-reference teaser: the narcotic would turn into another answer if one letter became a man's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Put TIM where the drug has its I and you get OPTIMUM, which means ideal, the answer to 3-down. The clue works backwards: take TIM out of OPTIMUM and put I in.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic made from the dried juice of poppy pods.

clue.text: Skip backward, and no plump chickens play

indicators.note: backward tells you to read the word from its last letter to its first

parts.note: to skip something is to omit it
'n' is the clipped form of and, as in rock 'n' roll
O is zero, nothing
plump means fat
hens are female chickens

explanation.surface: A children's game of skipping backwards with no fat poultry around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb about children's games; it is the noun, the Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is a tragedy by Shakespeare about a generous man turned bitter misanthrope.
